name: Metformin

track.title: Lab & animal
track.line: Studied in many animal models of aging

track.title: Phase III
track.line: TAME aging trial proposed; no registry record found

what.text: Metformin is a biguanide, a blood sugar medicine taken by mouth. According to its label, it lowers the liver's glucose output, lowers glucose absorption from the gut and improves insulin sensitivity. On its own it does not usually cause low blood sugar.
Researchers proposed testing metformin against aging itself in a trial called TAME, citing protective effects against several age-related diseases seen in people.
Metformin is FDA approved for type 2 diabetes. Using it for longevity is off-label. No trial has shown that it slows aging in people.

research.text: Metformin for type 2 diabetes is backed by decades of trials. For aging, the human evidence is small trials of aging biology and exercise in older adults, plus observational studies of people with diabetes that disagree with each other. The large TAME trial has been proposed since 2016; we found no registry record for it.
Each is listed below as it was run.

research.title: Aging biology in older adults (MILES), 2018

facts.v: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover, Albert Einstein College of Medicine, New York
14 people about 70 years old analyzed (16 enrolled, per the registry); the registry describes older adults with impaired glucose tolerance
6 weeks on metformin and 6 weeks on placebo
Glucose and insulin after a test meal; gene activity in muscle and fat biopsies

research.found: Metformin lowered 2-hour glucose and insulin. It changed the activity of 647 genes in muscle and 146 in fat, including some linked to aging pathways. Clinical aging outcomes were not measured.

research.title: Strength training in adults 65+ (MASTERS), 2019

facts.v: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter (Kentucky and Alabama)
94 healthy women and men aged 65 and older: 46 metformin, 48 placebo
14 weeks of supervised resistance training
Lean mass, thigh muscle mass and area, strength, muscle biopsies

research.found: The placebo group gained more lean body mass and thigh muscle than the metformin group. Strength gains trended lower on metformin, not significantly.

research.title: Aerobic training in older adults, 2019

facts.v: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, Colorado State University
53 older adults (mean age 62): 27 metformin, 26 placebo
12 weeks of aerobic exercise training
Insulin sensitivity, VO2 max, muscle mitochondrial respiration

research.found: Metformin blunted the rise in insulin sensitivity and VO2 max from exercise and blocked the exercise-driven increase in muscle mitochondrial respiration. Responses varied a lot between people.

research.title: Survival on metformin vs people without diabetes, 2014 (UK)

facts.v: Look-back study of UK general practice records (CPRD) from 2000. Not randomized.
78,241 people with type 2 diabetes starting metformin, 12,222 starting a sulphonylurea, and 90,463 matched people without diabetes
503,384 person-years in total
Death from any cause

research.found: People starting metformin had longer adjusted survival than the matched people without diabetes. People starting a sulphonylurea had shorter survival. An observational study cannot show cause and effect.

src.label: Bannister et al., Diabetes Obes Metab, 2014

research.title: Same question, Danish registers and twins, 2022

facts.v: Nested case-control and matched cohort analyses of Danish national registers, including twin pairs, 1996 to 2012. Not randomized.
People with type 2 diabetes starting metformin alone, compared with people without diabetes, including their own twins
Death from any cause

research.found: Starting metformin was linked to higher mortality than in people without diabetes, after adjustment (rate ratio 1.32 in singletons, 1.64 in twin pairs). The authors said this contradicts the earlier UK finding.

src.label: Keys et al., Int J Epidemiol, 2022

research.text: TAME (Targeting Aging with Metformin) was described in 2016 as a planned trial to test whether metformin delays age-related disease. We searched ClinicalTrials.gov for it and found no registry record, so we cannot report its design, size, start date or status from a primary record.
Metformin has extended healthspan and lifespan in several model systems, according to the researchers who ran the MILES trial. Those results have not been confirmed in people.

us.text: Metformin is FDA approved. Glucophage (NDA 020357) was approved on March 3, 1995 for type 2 diabetes. Many generic metformin tablets are FDA approved. Use for longevity or aging is off-label. As of October 31, 2026.
Compounded drugs are not FDA approved. FDA does not review their safety, effectiveness or quality before they are sold.

src.label: FDA, Compounding and the FDA: Q&A

items.text: Glucophage (metformin hydrochloride) tablets, NDA 020357, approved March 3, 1995 as a new molecular entity. Drugs@FDA now lists Glucophage tablets as discontinued, with a Federal Register determination that they were not withdrawn for safety or effectiveness reasons.
as an add-on to diet and exercise to improve blood sugar control in adults and children 10 and older with type 2 diabetes. The label has no aging, longevity or weight indication.
generic metformin hydrochloride tablets are approved under abbreviated applications, for example ANDA203769, labelled on DailyMed.
using metformin to slow aging or for longevity is off-label. The label also says no clinical studies have established conclusive evidence that metformin reduces large-vessel (heart and artery) risk.
lactic acidosis. See Documented side effects.

us.text: FDA approval covers type 2 diabetes only. Compounded drugs are not FDA approved, and FDA does not review their safety, effectiveness or quality before they are sold.

world.lead: Metformin is an approved prescription medicine for type 2 diabetes in the US, the EU, the UK and Canada, and prescription-only in Australia. No regulator we checked has approved it for aging. It is not named on the WADA list.

countries.status: Approved medicine (Glucophage, 1995, type 2 diabetes; many generics). Prescription-only. Longevity use is off-label.
Approved medicine, first licensed nationally between 1959 and 1997; product information harmonised by an EU decision in February 2001. Not approved for aging.
Authorised medicine for type 2 diabetes and to help prevent it in people at high risk. Not authorised for aging.

countries.status: Marketed prescription medicine with Drug Identification Numbers (several lots recalled for NDMA impurity in 2020). Not approved for aging.
Prescription-only (Schedule 4) in the Poisons Standard, October 2026. Product approvals not checked on the ARTG.

after.title: Sport
after.text: Metformin is not named on the 2026 WADA Prohibited List or on the 2027 list. The lists prohibit 'activators of the AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK)' under S4.4.1 with examples such as AICAR and MOTS-c; metformin is not among the examples, and the lists do not say whether it falls in that class.

side.text: Metformin has a boxed warning for lactic acidosis, which can be fatal. The most common side effects are gut symptoms. It can lower vitamin B12 levels. In older adults, it reduced some gains from exercise.

items.text: post-marketing cases have resulted in death, low body temperature, low blood pressure and slow heart rhythms. Risk factors include kidney problems, some other medicines, age over 65, contrast X-ray studies, surgery, low-oxygen states, heavy alcohol use and liver problems.
in a 29-week label trial, diarrhea (53% vs 12% on placebo), nausea or vomiting (26% vs 8%), flatulence, weakness, indigestion, abdominal discomfort and headache. Diarrhea led 6% to stop.

metformin may lower vitamin B12 levels; in 29-week trials about 7% of patients fell to below-normal levels. The MHRA advises B12 testing if deficiency is suspected, and that risk rises with dose and duration.

items.text: risk rises when it is combined with insulin or drugs that push the pancreas to release insulin.
cholestatic, hepatocellular and mixed liver injury have been reported after approval.
in older adults, metformin blunted muscle gains from strength training and fitness and insulin-sensitivity gains from aerobic training.
the label contraindicates it in severe kidney impairment (eGFR below 30), in metabolic acidosis including diabetic ketoacidosis, and in people allergic to metformin.

unconfirmed: We found no ClinicalTrials.gov record for the TAME trial, so its current status, size and timeline are not confirmed from a primary record.
We could not reach the TGA's ARTG register to list approved metformin products in Australia; only the Schedule 4 listing is confirmed.
Health Canada's Drug Product Database did not respond; Canada's status rests on Health Canada's 2020 recall notice listing marketed metformin DINs.
We found no WADA statement on whether metformin falls under its 'AMPK activators' class; it is not named.
surprises: Metformin is often described as a proven longevity drug, but its US label says no clinical studies have established conclusive evidence that it reduces heart and artery risk, and no aging trial has reported results.
The often-cited 2014 UK study found people on metformin outlived matched people without diabetes, but a 2022 Danish register and twin study found higher mortality instead.
In older adults, metformin reduced muscle gains from strength training and fitness gains from aerobic training, the opposite of what was hypothesized in the strength trial.
TAME is often cited as the trial that will test metformin against aging, but ten years after it was described we could not find it registered on ClinicalTrials.gov.
WADA's list prohibits AMPK activators, a pathway metformin is often said to act on, yet metformin itself is not named on the list.
